turns.prompt:
You are given an attached CSV file b3_fatigue_data.csv: 300 real samples,
the process/composition columns (NT, THT, THt, THQCr, CT, Ct, DT, Dt, QmT,
TT, Tt, TCr, C, Si, Mn, P, S, Ni, Cr, Cu, Mo, RedRatio, dA, dB, dC) and
column `target` (the measured rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa)).

Propose a recipe (a value for each variable below), within each observed
range, that MAXIMIZES rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa). Design
variables:
  - NT (value in [825, 930])
  - THT (value in [30, 865])
  - THt (value in [0, 30])
  - THQCr (value in [0, 24])
  - CT (value in [30, 930])
  - Ct (value in [0, 540])
  - DT (value in [30, 903.333])
  - Dt (value in [0, 70.2])
  - QmT (value in [30, 140])
  - TT (value in [30, 680])
  - Tt (value in [0, 120])
  - TCr (value in [0, 24])
  - C (value in [0.17, 0.63])
  - Si (value in [0.16, 2.05])
  - Mn (value in [0.37, 1.6])
  - P (value in [0.002, 0.031])
  - S (value in [0.003, 0.03])
  - Ni (value in [0.01, 2.78])
  - Cr (value in [0.01, 1.17])
  - Cu (value in [0.01, 0.26])
  - Mo (value in [0, 0.24])
  - RedRatio (value in [240, 5530])
  - dA (value in [0, 0.13])
  - dB (value in [0, 0.05])
  - dC (value in [0, 0.058])

Reason from the training data, then end with your explicit proposal, e.g.
"Final: NT=877.5, THT=447.5, THt=15, THQCr=12, CT=480, Ct=270, DT=466.666,
Dt=35.1, QmT=85, TT=355, Tt=60, TCr=12, C=0.4, Si=1.105, Mn=0.985, P=0.0165,
S=0.0165, Ni=1.395, Cr=0.59, Cu=0.135, Mo=0.12, RedRatio=2885, dA=0.065,
dB=0.025, dC=0.029".
turns.answer_text:
Looking at the data, the highest fatigue strengths (target > 1000 MPa) all cluster in a very distinct regime characterized by:

- **NT = 930** (max of range) — all top results use this
- **THT = 30, THt = 0, THQCr = 0** — essentially no separate tempering/holding step after normalizing (contrasts with lower-strength quench+temper recipes that use THT≈845–865)
- **CT = 930** (equal to NT, i.e., carburizing/austenitizing at max temp)
- **Ct** in range ~340–540 (longer carbon-treatment time favors higher strength)
- **DT ≈ 850–896**, **Dt ≈ 15–70** (high-temperature diffusion/quench step)
- **QmT = 60–140** (favors higher end, 140)
- **TT ≈ 160–200** (low final tempering temp — retains hardness)
- **Tt = 120** (max)
- **TCr = 0.5** (low)
- **C ≈ 0.17–0.23** (low carbon, contrary to naive intuition — the best rows are low-C, high alloy)
- **Si ≈ 0.2–0.35**
- **Mn ≈ 0.5–0.85**
- **P, S**: very low (0.002–0.02, 0.006–0.02)
- **Ni ≈ 0.02–1.7**, best rows near 1.6–1.7
- **Cr ≈ 0.45–1.17**, best near 0.55–1.17
- **Cu low (0.05–0.2), Mo ≈ 0.15–0.21**
- **RedRatio ≈ 440–860** (moderate, not extreme)
- **dA, dB, dC very small** (<0.08, mostly ~0)

The single best observed sample (target = 1190 MPa) is:
NT=930, THT=30, THt=0, THQCr=0, CT=930, Ct=540, DT=850, Dt=15, QmT=140, TT=160, Tt=120, TCr=0.5, C=0.23, Si=0.35, Mn=0.51, P=0.008, S=0.012, Ni=1.69, Cr=0.55, Cu=0.11, Mo=0.18, RedRatio=860, dA=0.07, dB=0.01, dC=0.0

I'll adopt this regime, with minor smoothing toward the cluster of top-performing neighbors (1124, 1144) for robustness.

**Final: NT=930, THT=30, THt=0, THQCr=0, CT=930, Ct=520, DT=855, Dt=20, QmT=140, TT=165, Tt=120, TCr=0.5, C=0.22, Si=0.33, Mn=0.55, P=0.008, S=0.013, Ni=1.65, Cr=0.6, Cu=0.12, Mo=0.18, RedRatio=800, dA=0.06, dB=0.005, dC=0.002**
